sections.body_md:
State feedback uses the whole state, not only the output. The law \(u = -Kx\) adds a rank-one update, and the closed-loop matrix is \(A - BK\). When the pair \((A, B)\) is reachable, that one row \(K\) can put every eigenvalue of \(A - BK\) on a polynomial you chose. The transient, the damping, and the natural frequency are then properties of the polynomial, not of the open-loop \(A\).

The same gain does not invent a new input direction. A mode that failed the rank test stays where \(A\) put it, for every \(K\). Placement is a statement about eigenvalues. It does not, by itself, make the steady error to a constant reference equal to zero.

sections.heading: Key equations
sections.body_md:
With a single input,
\[
\dot{x} = (A - BK) x, \qquad \det(sI - (A - BK)) = s^n + d_{n-1} s^{n-1} + \cdots + d_0.
\]
You pick the \(d_i\) from the desired poles, expand \(\det(sI - (A-BK))\) with the entries of \(K\) unknown, and match coefficients. For a reachable single-input pair the match has one solution. Ackermann's formula is that solution written as one product, using the desired polynomial and the controllability matrix. In controllable companion form the match is a subtraction: each open-loop coefficient is replaced by the desired one, scaled by the bottom entry of \(B\) when that entry is not 1.

sections.heading: Worked example
sections.body_md: Take \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ -2.4 & -0.7 \end{bmatrix}\) and \(B = \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1.6 \end{bmatrix}\). Ask for \(s^2 + 9.5 s + 18.2\). The closed-loop constant term is \(2.4 + 1.6 k_1\), and the coefficient of \(s\) is \(0.7 + 1.6 k_2\). Then \(1.6 k_1 = 15.8\), so \(k_1 = 9.875\), and \(1.6 k_2 = 8.8\), so \(k_2 = 5.5\). The factor \(1.6\) is the input scale. Dropping it would report \(15.8\) and \(8.8\), which are the gaps in the polynomial, not the gains.

sections.heading: Common pitfalls
sections.body_md: Writing \(u = +Kx\) flips every correction and solves the wrong sign. In companion form it is easy to match the constant term with the velocity gain and the \(s\) coefficient with the position gain; the constant term belongs to the gain on the undifferentiated state. A desired polynomial that is not monic, or that is written as \((s-p_1)(s-p_2)\) with the sign of a left-half-plane pole dropped, shifts every coefficient. And a short controllability rank does not become full rank because \(K\) has several entries.

sections.heading: Where this leads
sections.body_md: A constant reference still needs a path into the law, and a pure gain \(k_r\) sets the DC map without adding a state. An integrator on the tracking error is the later augmentation that removes a constant error. A quadratic cost picks one particular \(K\) instead of a hand-chosen polynomial. When the state is not measured, the same \(K\) is applied to an estimate, and the closed-loop eigenvalues split into the ones you placed here and the ones the estimator placed.
